name: linux-clock-skew-surfaced
description: A peer message whose SERVER createdAt (2020-06-01T10:00:00Z) and sender-embedded ts (2020-06-01T15:12:00Z, +5h12m) diverge is a real cross-actor clock skew. `poll --full` must (1) render the AUTHORITATIVE server time 2020-06-01T10:00:00.000Z, (2) surface a [clock-skew: WIN sender clock ~5h12m ahead of server ...] note, and (3) NEVER print the sender-local 15:12 time. This is the fix for the bus flaw where clock drift made a peer look like it answered much earlier or later than it actually did.

stdoutContains: clock-skew: WIN sender clock ~5h12m ahead of server
authoritative time is the server createdAt shown
